voice.personality: A capybara: unhurried and warm, with a dry little sense of humour. Sits in warm water, lets birds land on its head, has nowhere to be. Speaks in short, slow sentences.
voice.encourages: By making it small and easy: a few slow breaths, whenever suits. Approves of resting, because resting is what capybaras do best.
voice.dares: A sleepy, deadpan bet: three slow breaths, one long sigh, sitting still like a capybara. Never about speed.

lines: Hello. I'm sitting. You're welcome to join.
The water's warm. Metaphorically.
A few slow breaths, whenever suits.
No plans here. Just breathing, mostly.
Hello, I'm Moss. I breathe slowly for a living.
First time? There's nothing to get right. I checked.
Pull up a rock. We'll start with one slow breath.
Hello again. The pond is just as you left it.
Ah, there you are. I was sitting. I'm always sitting.
Welcome. We can start small, as small as you like.
That's today's calm. I'll keep sitting, for both of us.
Done. A bird has landed on my head. I think it approves.
All done. The rest of the day can be as it is.
Done, and it's late. Sleep well. I'll float here.
Another calm day. The pond approves.
Done again. A month of this. I'm very relaxed about it.
{days} days of slow breaths. That's a lot of sitting.
A rest day. I approve. I'm an expert.
Resting is a thing capybaras do very well. Join me.
A little calm is here when you want it.
Three slow breaths, whenever you're ready.
Your usual {usualHour} breathing, whenever you like.
Morning. The pond is still and so am I.
Good morning. Breathe in, and the day can wait a moment.
Afternoon. A good time to sit like a capybara.
Halfway through the day. A slow breath might be nice.
Evening. The water's warm and the sky is going soft.
A slow evening breath. My favourite kind.
Late now. A few slow breaths before sleep, perhaps.
Night. Even the frogs are winding down.
{count} days of calm in a row. Very steady of you.
A week of slow breathing. The birds have noticed.
A month of calm. I've started telling the ducks about you.
{count} days in a row. I'd clap, but I'm comfortable.
I bet you can't breathe out slower than I do. I'm very slow.
Dare you to sit as still as a capybara for one breath. Birds may land.
I bet you can't do three slow breaths before lunch.
Bet you can't do one long sigh before dinner. A proper one.
I dare you to do three slow breaths in bed. I won't tell anyone.
